name: Jaasiel
overview: Jaasiel was a male figure from the tribe of Benjamin who served as a chief officer for the Benjaminites. He is identified specifically as the son of Abner. The biblical record of Jaasiel is concise, focusing on his leadership role within his tribe.
namesAndTitles: The name Jaasiel means 'G-d [El] does,' reflecting a theophoric element common in Hebrew names. This proper name does not indicate that it was given directly by God but carries a meaning that acknowledges divine action.
familyAndRelationships: Jaasiel is explicitly recorded as the son of Abner. Beyond this father-son relationship, Scripture does not provide additional family details for Jaasiel.
scriptureSignificance: Jaasiel's significance lies in his leadership capacity as a chief officer among the Benjaminites, a role that implies responsibility and authority within his tribe. His identification as Abner's son connects him to a notable family line within the tribe of Benjamin. This brief mention preserves his place in the organizational structure of Israel during the period recorded in 1 Chronicles.
